A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SVS research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison; rendered-page inspection resolves text-extraction ordering artifacts.

before.justification: v1 reports original SVS and RLVR training experiments, reasoning and general-task benchmark results, entropy trajectories, and Pass@k analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds controlled comparisons, synthesis-training ablations, learning-curve analyses, and generated-response case studies.

M1.justification: The proposed SVS procedure retains solution-conditioned problem synthesis, reuse of original reference answers, difficulty-based synthesis rewards, and joint training on three experience types. The relocated algorithm and expanded walkthrough document the existing method; the new experimental variants do not replace it.

E1.justification: Both versions use MATH-12k, DAPO-17k, the DeepMath supplement, and the same mathematical, general-question-answering, and coding benchmarks. The new IID/OOD analysis groups existing benchmarks by answer format; it does not introduce new data or task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 Table 3 adds a substantive alternative-strategy comparison: extended RLVR training (Ext), additional rollouts on underperforming problems (Eup), and easier-problem augmentation (SvS-Asp). These controls were absent from v1. The original Table 1 comparators, including SimpleRL-32B and ORZ-32B, remain.

E3.justification: The new Table 3 experiments match total problem-solution pairs for Ext or per-step pairs for Eup, test a 37.5%–75.0% augmentation-accuracy range, and select checkpoints by average AIME 24/25 scores. Section 5.4 adds a condition using only 20% of synthesis pairs for updates and reports grouped IID/OOD accuracy. Previously stated default settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds training-volume controls, easier-problem and synthesis-fraction ablations, response-length analysis, benchmark learning trajectories, and detailed response/workflow cases. These substantially expand investigation of why SVS works. The instance-level accuracy analysis already shown in v1 Figure 7 is retained as v3 Figure 9, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 32-generation Pass@1 averaging, unbiased Pass@k estimation, and the 1024-generation instance-level comparison. No new training-seed information, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the general-task table retain their scores, but substantial results are added. v3 Table 3 reports average Pass@1/Pass@32 of 24.6/46.3 for Ext, 21.7/50.9 for Eup, and 22.8/42.8 for SvS-Asp, alongside retained full-SVS scores of 27.9/53.1. Figure 7 adds worse OOD performance with reduced synthesis training; appendices add response-length, checkpoint, and case outcomes.

T1.justification: The GRPO definitions and objective move from v1 Section 3.1 to v3 Appendix A, while SVS reward definitions remain mathematically equivalent. No new theorem, proof, or formal guarantee is introduced. Mathematical workings in the new cases are sampled model responses, not new theoretical contributions.

C1.justification: The central claims remain annotation-free self-play, sustained entropy and diversity, improved large-k reasoning performance, and generality across 3B–32B models and 12 reasoning benchmarks. The abstract retains the same 18.3- and 22.8-point AIME Pass@32 gains; new analyses support these retained contributions.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's entropy explanation and integer-answer overfitting discussion, v3 interprets additional negative samples as encouraging exploration, easier-problem augmentation as accelerating overfitting, and synthesis training as regularization through complementary generation and solving tasks. Appendix D and the cases further connect longer responses and systematic reasoning to continued exploration, substantially expanding the mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies Clip-Higher epsilon as 0.28 and explicitly describes the baseline training recipe. Appendix F supplies a separate problem-solving prompt display, and the first-page project-site address changes. Most learning-rate, batch-size, sampling, training-duration, and verification details were already reported in v1 and are relocated.

R1.justification: v3 adds targeted context, including Cheng et al. (2024) as closely related self-play work, dual learning for the regularization explanation, and ProRL for prolonged training. It also adds latent-reasoning citations and a reference for the already evaluated SimpleRL baseline. The overall research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: GRPO background, pseudocode, and detailed settings move into Appendices A–C, accompanied by an expanded algorithm walkthrough and appendix contents page. The analysis narrative gains separate controls and mechanism sections, while contributions are consolidated and terminology edited. Sentence-level rewriting of retained scientific passages is mostly light.

P2.justification: v3 adds an ablation table, synthesis-fraction plots, response-length and benchmark learning curves, and case displays. Existing tables are packed together, Figures 2 and 5 are redrawn with smoothing, the instance-level plot is relocated and recolored, and the synthesis prompt is restyled. New Figure 8 incorrectly labels response-length axes as Policy Entropy.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked controls addressing whether SVS gains merely reflected additional training examples and how synthesis training contributed. v3 Table 3's training-pair-matched alternatives and Section 5.4's synthesis ablation directly address these important evidence gaps, substantially strengthening support for the retained claims. Expanded walkthroughs improve transparency. Remaining uncertainty-reporting limitations and minor editorial defects, including Figure 8's mislabeled axes, do not outweigh these gains.
